title: 3 Anime to Watch If You’re Waiting for Re:Zero Season 5
content:
Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World – is easily one of the biggest anime on Crunchyroll, and it continues to get more popular thanks to its sequel seasons. 2026 was a huge year for fans since the anime not only commemorated its 10th anniversary , but also aired its Season 4 in two cours. Written by Tappei Nagatsuki, Re:Zero is one of the most intense dark fantasies that doesn’t shy away from showing the brutalities of the world Subaru is forced to live in. The fourth season was one of the biggest anime of the year as it continues Subaru’s gruesome journey where he is forced to witness his friends die in gruesome ways, forcing him to realize his own weakness.

The latest season ended on a massive cliffhanger as it wraps up the Pleiades Watchtower storyline. Luckily, the anime has already confirmed a fifth season that will follow Subaru’s journey to the Vollachian Empire. The story will continue to be more intense from here on out, and the creator has confirmed that fans can expect new encounters along the way. The fifth season hasn’t shared a release window yet, so there’s no guarantee how long we have to wait for the anime’s return. In the meantime, if you’re looking for more anime to watch, then you’ll definitely love these three as a fan of Re:Zero .

3) Steins;Gate

Steins;Gate is one of the highest-rated psychological anime of all time. First released as a visual novel in 2009, the franchise would receive an anime adaptation in 2011 that helped spread this incredible story all across the world. As a time-travel anime involving deep emotional connections and the consequences of such a power, Steins;Gate is highly addictive, especially if you love layers of mysteries.

At first, the prospect of time travel might seem like an exciting breakthrough, but it soon becomes clear through cycles of psychological torment that not everything is as it seems on the surface. The same animation studio behind Re:Zero also worked on Steins;Gate , and both stories focus on time-travelling protagonists. While both stories have different narrative structures, they focus on the traumatizing consequences for the protagonists and their loved ones as the repeating tragedies cost them their sanity.

2) Summer Time Rendering

Anime shows centering around the themes of time travel or time loops are scarce, but whenever such a story is released, it immediately piques viewers’ interest. The reason this anime stands out is thanks to the premiere episode that contains just the right amount of mystery and action to hook viewers, but doesn’t answer all the questions right away. The anime wraps up the story in just 25 episodes, which is significantly less compared to the 139 chapters of the manga. However, since the manga chapters are rather short, the anime did manage to cover the entire story with fast pacing and minor cuts from the original.

Thanks to the quick pacing, each episode keeps the viewers on the edge of their seats as they look forward to what’s going to happen next. The story centers around Shinpei Ajiro, who returns to his hometown after the sudden death of his childhood friend. He stumbles upon the dangers lurking in the seemingly peaceful island that might be related to the recent tragedy. Amid all the chaos and confusion, he realizes he has the power to time loop after he dies, which is pretty much the same as the ability Subaru has.

1) Puella Magi Madoka Magica

While Puella Magi Madoka Magica isn’t an isekai series and it doesn’t have a protagonist who can time travel, fans of Re:Zero will love this dark fantasy nonetheless. This acclaimed fantasy classic on Crunchyroll is a surprisingly gruesome psychological thriller that hides behind its cheerful and bright animation style. With one glance at the anime and the adorable magical girls, no one could ever imagine the true horrors awaiting viewers. This award-winning show premiered its anime series in 2011 before returning with sequel movies in 2012 and 2013 .

This original story centers around Madoka Kaname and Sayaka Miki, two middle school girls whose ordinary lives take drastic turns after encountering Kyuubey, a mysterious magical familiar. While the girls accept the offer to gain magical powers, they never realize it comes with a steep price. Before they knew it, Kyuubey forces them into a no-win systematic trap where they must do whatever they can to end the suffering of all the magical girls who fell for the brutal trap.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime you’d like to recommend that shares similar vibes to Re:Zero ? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Solo Leveling Doesn’t Deserve the Hype Because of One Fatal Flaw
content:
Even before the anime debuted in 2024, Solo Leveling was globally popular thanks to the exceptional story written by Chugong. The light novel and the webtoon’s success, along with the stunning visuals by A-1 Pictures, made it possible for the anime adaptation to reach new heights of popularity. While the novel and the webtoon are already concluded, the anime still has a huge chunk of story left to adapt. The second season was released in Winter last year, and it wasn’t until July this year that a sequel movie was announced . While fans know almost nothing about the anime sequel, the only thing that’s confirmed at this point is that it’s going to be another massive success.

However, while the series has countless fans, the number of haters can’t be ignored either. The series is often criticized for a number of reasons, including the fact that it ignores a lot of character depth, among many other things. For a series as popular as Solo Leveling , it receives just as much hate for always being in the spotlight. Although it’s completely subjective to like or hate the series, it does have its weak points that make the criticisms valid. While Solo Leveling is far from the best series , it’s not nearly as boring as many would claim it to be. However, there is one fatal flaw that makes the series deserving of its overhyped reputation.

Solo Leveling ‘s Greatest Weakness Is Its Wasted World-Building Potential

There’s no denying that Solo Leveling ‘s world-building could have been one of the best in the webtoon industry. The story takes place in an urban fantasy world where mysterious gates showed up out of nowhere. As if that wasn’t enough, it also blends video game rules through the system , which is directly tied to the historic event that changed the world. While the main story itself takes place in a realistic setting, Jinwoo often travels through dimensions to level up, which is why we keep seeing all kinds of different settings.

Not only that, but the world-building continues to expand after he uncovers the secret about the System. The story features the world through his lens and tries its best to focus on the juxtaposition of the modern setting and the alternate fantasy realms that are directly tied to it. In theory, the world-building seems flawless, but the story barely manages to hold up to its true potential. The initial idea behind the world-building was great, but somewhere between the fast-paced story and the intense action, the world-building never truly had a chance to shine.

World-building is more than just the setting of the story and the places it features, but it also includes the history, society, characters, the power system, and more. Whether it’s the historic cosmic war or the side characters, the series could have done a lot with the world-building, but never truly had the opportunity. Whether it’s a real-world setting with gates, monsters, and guilds, it’s obvious that all these things were only there for surface-level build-up. It also doesn’t help that the story focuses way too much on Jinwoo, even to the point of neglecting just about any other character besides him. This includes the villains and the supporting characters since rarely anyone had the chance to shine with Jinwoo grabbing all the attention.

Solo Leveling Is Popular Mostly Because of Its Intense Fights

Solo Leveling relies on a straightforward story with lots of action , the protagonist’s power-up, and the constant threat he keeps facing. The only reason the series actually works is that it’s a simplistic portrayal of an urban fantasy that doesn’t try to appear too deep or complex. It’s the kind of show you can read or watch for fun without thinking too deeply about the state of the world and characters. Because the story is fast-paced, the viewers’ attention remains on the protagonist, so you wouldn’t expect much from the political intrigue and the social setting it introduced.

Instead of focusing on heavy lore, the series relies on methodical progression to help Jinwoo reach the top as soon as possible. The only redeeming quality that sets Solo Leveling apart from other series is the intense battles Jinwoo has fought throughout his journey. As an action series, it nails the fight choreography even in the webtoon thanks to the incredible illustrations by DUBU. However, the animation studio elevates them even further with fluid sequences as it relies on the story’s only strength. It’s not really surprising that Solo Leveling is the best when it comes to webtoon adaptations, and it’s easily the best series from A-1 Pictures studio.

Do you think Solo Leveling could have been even better without this fatal flaw? In your opinion, what is the one thing the series is missing the most? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: Sakamoto Days Ends With Shonen Jump’s Best 2026 Finale
content:
Out of all five major Shonen Jump manga series that ended in 2026, Sakamoto Days had the best ending. 2026 has been a very important year for the manga and anime industry, witnessing several revolutionary changes and making a significant impact on the entertainment industry as a whole. In the manga world, Shueisha’s Shonen Jump magazine continues to be a leading force, producing many great manga series, several of which have come to an end this year. This is precisely because of how the magazine is embracing a new style, which has also brought about numerous changes. Among the different ways the magazine has evolved, it has also seen five major Shonen Jump series come to an end.

It all started with Jujutsu Kaisen ‘s sequel, Modulo , coming to an early end in March, followed by Chainsaw Man ‘s sudden conclusion in the same month, which took fans by surprise. Next, Black Clover , a series that had been running for more than 11 years, came to an end in July, followed by Blue Box . Sakamoto Days was also expected to end this year, as it had been in its final phase since last July. On November 22, the series finally came to a halt. However, out of all five Shonen Jump series that ended this year , Sakamoto Days has proven to have the best ending.

Sakamoto Days ‘ Ending Fits Its Original Premise Better Than Most Manga Endings

What makes Sakamoto Days ‘ ending better than those of the other major Shonen Jump series that ended in 2026 isn’t that it does something exceptional, but that it fits its original premise better than the others. In that regard, Modulo and Chainsaw Man don’t even come close, as both series have controversial endings, especially the latter. Fans are still hoping for a Chainsaw Man sequel that will fill in the gaps left by the elements the series missed. Meanwhile, Black Clover has arguably the most clichéd shonen ending, which makes it a perfect conclusion in its own way, but it was also predictable, and something fans could be content with. As for Blue Box , it closed the chapter on Taiki and Chono’s high school years.

Arguably, Blue Box had the potential to stand out the most among them, but its ending ultimately focuses on closing this chapter while hinting at something even bigger and better ahead. Sakamoto Days , meanwhile, manages to end with enigmatic battle action that most shonen series cannot match. Its titular character is an assassin who can adapt to any situation, using everyday objects around him as weapons, making his fights unpredictable and often hilarious. Sakamoto and Slur’s final battle is a testament to this. However, what takes it a step further is how the fight aligns with Sakamoto’s identity as a family man.

Sakamoto using everyday household items to highlight that he is a husband and father is one of the most unique actions any shonen series has featured in years . It perfectly matches the importance of family that the series has represented since its beginning. As for the actual conclusion, the series ends in the best comical way possible, with its characters fitting perfectly into the story’s structure.

These final moments stay true to what the series has always been about, avoiding anything overly grand or confusing and actually bringing things to a close. That is what makes Sakamoto Days the major manga series of 2026 that sticks the landing better than the other four series that also ended this year. How do you feel about Sakamoto Days ending? Where does it rank among your favorites of the year? Let us know in the comments.

title: Dragon Ball Super Will Never Evolve Without Going Beyond Dragon Ball Z’s Ending
content:
As long as Dragon Ball Super remains stuck within the ten year gap of time before the end of Dragon Ball Z , the story is never truly going to have the amount of freedom to explore its potential as fans might want. Dragon Ball series creator Akira Toriyama sadly passed away back in 2024, and it’s left the franchise in a holding pattern ever since. While there is a new anime airing its episodes this Fall , and another now in the works, these releases aren’t moving the story forward.

Dragon Ball Super’ s manga has been on hiatus for the past couple of years without any signs of returning anytime soon , and it’s likely because those currently behind the franchise are still trying to figure out a path forward. The rights for the Dragon Ball series are in flux as many notable studios and figures are in the mix, but once that’s all settled it’ll be time to move the story forward. But it’s never going to be the kind of series fans might want as there’s still an ending to eventually adhere too.

Dragon Ball Super Needs to Be Able to Continue the Timeline

Dragon Ball Super has unfortunately sparked all kinds of timeline debates and confusion among fans ever since Toriyama returned to continue Dragon Ball Z ‘s story with the Battle of Gods arc. While the end of the manga imagined a future ten years after the end of the Majin Buu arc, Battle of Gods began to introduce new adventures within that span of time. While this had been an exciting prospect at the start, the more Dragon Ball Super continues the more it’s apparent that it’s eventually going to hit a brick wall as to how far it can actually go .

The Battle of Gods arc opened up the Dragon Ball franchise to an entirely new multiverse of ideas with 12 new universes full of potential allies or foes, Gods of Destruction that were the strongest beings of their respective universes, Angels that are even stronger than the Gods, and more as the scale and scope of everything increased dramatically from where Dragon Ball Z originally ended. Yet despite how much more infinitely the franchise can grow from this point on, it still technically has to fit within that ten year gap of time. It can never go beyond that ending.

Dragon Ball Super can never truly expand on some of its best ideas because it can never be a true sequel to Dragon Ball Z . Fans might continue to debate whether or not Dragon Ball GT was a successful attempt to continue the story without Toriyama, but unfortunately the franchise finds itself within that same situation once more as it moves on with new releases without its creator. And at least when it comes to Dragon Ball GT, it was able to move the timeline forward with its take on Goku and ability to play with ideas like Goku training Uub.

Dragon Ball Super Can Finally Fix Its Timeline

Working within this ten year time gap also puts an unnecessary limiter on what Dragon Ball can actually do with any of its future projects. It’s why even Toriyama approved and created releases like Dragon Ball Daima ended up being marred by all sorts of other debates. It was a release also set right after the events of the Majin Buu arc, and that constraint just opened up a can of worms about which of the events were actually part of the canon even if they technically all are.

If the franchise has any hope for a future, it needs to be able to actually move into that future . Without Toriyama around, all of these Dragon Ball projects are going to technically both be a part of the canon and not at the same time anyway. But if Dragon Ball Super is finally able to move forward beyond End of Z and become a true sequel, then the literal sky is the limit for what it can do with Goku and all of the other characters. There will always be a ceiling on it otherwise.

That just seems antithetical to the Dragon Ball idea. It originally began with a young boy setting out on a magical adventure filled with possibilities and no limits on how far he could go. It eventually ended with the idea that Goku can pursue godly levels of strength heading into the future, but as is, he’ll never truly be able to break that ceiling. There’s only so much Dragon Ball can do right now as long as it continues to adhere by that unnecessary limit.

What do you want to see from Dragon Ball Super next? Do you want to keep the end of the timeline as is? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Jujutsu Kaisen Studio’s Next Shonen Jump Anime Shares New Look Ahead of Jump Festa 2027
content:
The studio behind hits such as Jujutsu Kaisen, Attack on Titan and more has a new Shonen Jump anime coming our way next year, and has dropped a new look at it ahead of its next big update during Jump Festa 2027 later this December. Shueisha’s annual event is set to reveal a whole bunch of updates about all of the new anime and manga projects they have in the works for the next year and beyond, and that means we’re about to get many new releases confirmed too.

title: Major Horror Anime Drops New Opening Ahead of Netflix Debut – Watch Now
content:
A cool new horror thriller is set to make its anime debut with Netflix later this week, and has dropped its official opening theme sequence early to help celebrate its premiere. This series might be missing out on the horror holiday season, but thankfully it’s helping to boost up the final stretch of the Fall 2026 anime schedule . Fool Night is a new anime adaptation of Kasumi Yasuda’s original manga, and it’s going to be taken on with two of the biggest anime studios around.

Fool Night is a post-apocalyptic series set in a world where there is such a lack of oxygen , people end up planting seeds within their body to keep the little flow of it there is left. It’s likely going to be a solid thriller to cap off the year with, and thankfully it won’t be too much longer before we see it in action. Fool Night has released its creditless opening theme titled “Shake! spit out” as performed by Tempalay ahead of the anime’s debut, and you can check it out below.

Fool Night Releases New Opening Ahead of Netflix Premiere

Fool Night will be making its worldwide debut with Netflix on November 26th, and will be running for 12 episodes. All of those episodes will be available to watch at the time of release, and the ending theme for the series titled “Iki” as performed by Nowlu. It’s going to be a pretty big project too as it’s a joint collaboration between two of the biggest anime studios, Sunrise (which has overseen franchises like Mobile Suit Gundam ) and Shaft (known for releases like Puella Magi Madoka Magica ).

Atsuyuki Yukawa is directing the new Fool Night anime for Sunrise and Shaft with Ryo Shimura serving as assistant director, Jin Tanaka handling the series composition, Robert Sato providing the character designs, and Tatsuya Kato composing the music. The voice cast for the anime includes Koki Uchiyama as Toshiro Kamiya, Minako Kotobuki as Yomiko Horai, Junya Enoki as Akira Yatsuka, Aya Endo as Saeko Kanaeno, Kiyomitsu Mizuuchi as Jin Hiragishi, Shion Wakayama as Sumi Matsuno, Hiroshi Tsuchida as Ken Hikasa, Nobuhiko Okamoto as Nishi, Sayaka Senbongi as Meg Okumura, and Yumiko Kobayashi as Ivy.

What to Know for Fool Night ‘s Anime

Fool Night will also be debuting with an English dub release when it makes its way to Netflix , and it’s going to be spearheaded by the likes of Adam McArthur as Toshiro and Olivia Liang as Yomiko but the majority of the cast has yet to be confirmed as of this time. The series is a darker post-apocalyptic tale with an interesting take on the world as the anime introduces an idea known as “Transfloration,” where those dying plant seeds in their bodies to produce more oxygen.

It’s been a weaker year for horror anime in general despite some standout releases, but this could end up bridging the gap thanks to its science fiction appeal. With it debuting on Netflix this week, it won’t be too much longer before we see what it has to offer. How are you feeling about the new Fool Night anime so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Historie Anime Reveals New Visual, Trailer Additional Cast
content:
The previously announced Historie anime revealed a new visual and trailer on Wednesday along with additional voice cast members. Studio LIDEN FILMS is animating the series, set to premiere in January 8, 2027. The addtional cast includes:

• Fumihiko Tachiki as Antigonus

• Akira Sekine as Satura

• Toshiki Masuda as Bato

• Ryota Takeuchi as Dimakos

• Seiichiro Yamashita as Telemakos

The opening theme song “Masshiro” is performed by yorushika performs the anime’s opening theme song (Pure White), which is also previewed in the above video. RETRORIRON is performing the anime’s ending theme song “Amphoria.” The voice cast for the anime includes:

• Nobunaga Shimazaki as Eumenes

• Ryota Suzuki as Hieronymous

• Kazuya Ichijo as Hieronymous the Elder

• Yuko Kaida as Telesilla

• Wataru Takagi as Charon

• Satoshi Tsuruoka as Hecateus

• Anri Katsu as Thrax

• Tsuguo Mogami as Aristotle

• Miki Kariya as Perialla

• Seiyu Fujiwara as Nicogenes

• Junya Enoki as Tolmides

Nobuharu Kamanaka is directing the anime with Takatoshi Suzuki as the assistant director. Toshiya Ono is in charge of the scripts while, Isoroku Koga is illustrating character designs and is credited as chief animation director. Gin Hashiba is composing the music.

The Historie (stylized as HISTORIĒ ) manga by Hitoshi Iwaaki has been serialized in Kodansha’s Monthly Afternoon magazine since January 2003, releasing a total of 12 volumes as of June 2024.

Historie received the Grand Prize at the 14th Japan Media Arts Festival in 2010, the 16th Tezuka Osamu Cultural Prize in 2012, as well as the 49th Kodansha Manga Award in the general category in 2025.

The manga is available in English at K MANGA , where the story is described: A historical epic set in ancient times, Historie tells the story of Eumenes, a young man with quick wits and a vast destiny to fulfill. In time, he’ll become a famed army commander and personal secretary to Alexander the Great—but the road to this glory is fraught with danger…

title: Black Clover Season 2 Shocks With Sudden Love Confession
content:
Black Clover is reaching the final stretch of its episodes for Season 2 this year, but the latest episode really took fans by surprise with a sudden confession of love. Black Clover Season 2 has been working its way through the adaptation of the Spade Kingdom Raid arc from Yuki Tabata’s original manga, and each new episodes brings the fights against the Dark Triad one step closer to their end. And the latest episode explored the fallout of the fight against Megicula we had seen before .

Black Clover Season 2 recently wrapped up the fight with Megicula, and it came with some major developments for Noelle Silva during the midst of it. The fight saw her realizing that she really has romantic feelings for Asta for the first real time , but the newest episode threw even her for a loop as another relationship is developing instead between Lolopechka and Gaja thanks to his sudden confession of love.

Black Clover Season 2 Confirms Lolopechka and Gaja Romance

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 8 explores the immediate fallout of the fight with Megicula. It had seemed like Gaja had fully sacrificed himself, but Mimosa Vermillion arrived just in time to heal his fatal injuries. With Lolopechka also being freed from the Supreme Devil’s curse, it was the first reunion between the two since they were last seen in the anime five years ago. Gaja had been fighting to rescue Lolopechka after she had been kidnapped from the Heart Kingdom, and wasted no time with her reunion with her at last.

Gaja fully confessed his feelings of love to Lolopechka, and it seems like the two of them are going to happily move forward with their new relationship. With how many of these types of romantic connections that have been seen in Black Clover so far, it makes a great deal of difference to see that a relationship is actually moving forward. It’s not just someone hiding their crush on someone else through wacky understandings, and hopefully it could inspire Noelle to move forward with her own crush.

What’s Next for Black Clover Season 2?

Black Clover Season 2 has yet to confirm how many episodes it’s going to be sticking around for, but it’s been made even more apparent with the latest episodes that it’s going to be wrapping up its run later this year. The season has already seen two members of the Dark Triad being defeated, and the next one is close at hand . There aren’t many fights left in the arc to explore from this point, so fans should get ready for the climax hitting sooner rather than later.

Black Clover is also leading towards its adaptation of the final arc from Yuki Tabata’s original manga sooner rather than later, but it’s likely going to be in a future season yet to come. But that’s all yet to be officially confirmed one way or the other, so it’s best to catch up with Season 2 now streaming with Crunchyroll to see what could be coming on the way next.

What did you think of Black Clover’ s latest confession in Season 2’s newest episode? How are you liking the new season so far? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Link Click Season 3 Confirms 2027 Return for Part 2 With New Look
content:
Link Click confirms a 2027 release window for Season 3 Part 2. Crunchyroll brought back the new season of this beloved series in August this year as part of the Summer 2026 anime lineup. As the largest streaming platform for anime fans across the globe, Crunchyroll is home to several acclaimed shows and movies, including Donghua, a term used for Chinese animation . The industry has been on the rise for the past few years, with Link Click being one of the most notable series thanks to its global availability on Crunchyroll. The donghua is based on an original story, and it centers around mind-bending mysteries while blending supernatural themes.

The story has always been kind of intense and heartbreaking, but things have taken a turn for the worse in the latest season. The first part of Season 3 reached its conclusion last weekend, and the anime confirmed the release window of Part 2 right away. Fans also got the first look at the second part and everything else we can expect from the story going forward. The official YouTube channel of Bilibili shared the second part’s trailer while the official X handle dropped a new key visual.

What Is the Release Date of Link Click Season 3 Part 2?

Link Click Season 3 Part 2 has confirmed a 2027 release window, and the anime is expected to premiere in the second half of next year. However, the exact release date won’t be announced anytime soon. Link Click doesn’t always follow the quarterly schedule on Crunchyroll, where all anime series are released around the first two weeks of the month after TV broadcast in Japan.

While most of the Summer anime are released in July, Link Click released its third season a month later, and it’s quite possible the anime will follow a similar schedule this time as well. Additionally, we can expect the anime to return on Crunchyroll, where you can also find all the episodes.

Link Click Season 3 Part 2 Will Be More Intense Than Ever

The trailer is more than enough to convince fans that the upcoming season will be more gruesome than ever, where Lu Guang will face a major threat to his life. The story doesn’t shy away from taking fans on an emotional rollercoaster with the dark themes and heart-wrenching tragedies, and the latest season has made it clear that things will only continue to get worse.

The key visual also highlights the true extent of the horrors that Xiaoshi and Guang will keep facing from here on out, as they stand in front of several corpses. Needless to say, the situation appears to be far worse than anything they both have ever faced so far. Additionally, we can also expect more plot twists in the upcoming episodes that will completely turn the lives of everyone in Time Studio upside down.

Are you caught up with all episodes of Link Click on Crunchyroll? Head down to the comments to let us know your expectations for Season 3 Part 2.

title: The Kept Man of the Princess Knight Anime Reveals New Trailer, Additional Cast, January 3 Premiere
content:
The Kept Man of the Princess Knight anime revealed a new trailer, additional cast and a January 3, 2027 premiere date. Additionally, sajou no hana sings the ending theme song “Gika.” The additional cast consists of:

• Yuya Hirose as Ralph

• Manaka Iwami as Noel

• Shion Wakayama as Beatrice

• Saori Onishi as Cecilia

Studio BLADE is animating with Chihiro Kumano as director. Deko Akao is writing the script while Hisao Ishii is designing the characters. The cast includes:

• Junichi Suwabe as Matthew

• Mikako Komatsu as Arwin

• Rie Takahashi as Vanessa

• Tetsu Inada as Dezu

• Rika Nagae as April

The Kept Man of the Princess Knight is a Japanese light novel series written by Toru Shirogane and illustrated by Saki Mashima. The series began publication under ASCII Media Works’ Dengeki Bunko imprint on February 10, 2022. There is also a manga adaptation by Keyyang, began serialization on Kadokawa’s ComicWalker manga website in September 2022. It got three volumes after which a sequel by Chihiro Yamazaki titled The Kept Man of the Princess Knight Act2 began on August 31, 2025. Yen Press is publishing the series in English, describing the light novel as: The Dungeon City is a wicked place filled with crime, debauchery, and death. Its one shining light is Arwin, the beautiful Crimson Princess Knight. She and her brave party of adventurers descend into the dungeon at the city’s center, seeking a legendary treasure with the power to rebuild the princess’s fallen kingdom. Many yearn to be by her side, but that spot is already taken by Matthew, a man despised by all in town as a cowardly weakling. Everyone thinks he is scum who just spends her hard-earned money on booze, women, and gambling. No one in the city—not even the princess knight— knows what Matthew is truly capable of. Source: The Kept Man of the Princess Knight anime Official Website ©Toru Shirogane, KADOKAWA / The Kept Man of the Princess Knight Production Committee
